newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MOSTLY EASIER IN BRISK TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MOSTLY EASIER IN BRISK TRADE.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were indicated stable to weaker in brisk trade on Wednesday with demand for treasury bills continuing high, dealers said.

"The market is still very active. There are a lot of maturities and there is speculation that rates will come down, so everyone is looking for 30 and 60 day treasury bills (to sell at a profit later)," one dealer commented.
Treasury bills were being traded on the market at 17.50 percent, slightly down from 17.80 percent the previous day.

The buying and selling rates for 30, 60 and 90-day NCD bills were unchanged at 19.50 and 18.25 percent respectively, while bankers acceptance bills were quoted steady at 18.25 percent (buying) but softer at 17.75 from 17.85 percent (selling).
Call money was also easier at 17 percent from Tuesday's 18 percent, with the central Reserve Bank indicating a market surplus of Z$413 million at settlement.
